title: Review a refactor whose diff says every line changed
summary: Code was moved, reindented and renamed in one commit. The default diff is unreadable. Four flags turn it into a review you can actually do — and one of them belongs in your global config.
mental_model: A diff is computed, not stored, so you can ask for a different one at any time. The default algorithm optimises for size, not for human reading — the flags below trade a little computation for a diff that reflects what actually happened.

commit.message: Reorder functions and add a timeout check

steps.title: The diff nobody can review
steps.why: One real change — a new timeout check — hidden inside a wholesale reordering. The default diff reports far more churn than actually happened, because it optimises for a small diff rather than a meaningful one.
steps.expect: Large removed and added blocks that are mostly the same code in a different place.

steps.title: Count the noise
steps.why: `--numstat` gives added and removed line counts per file, machine-readably. Establish the baseline number before trying to reduce it — this is how you tell whether a flag actually helped.
steps.expect: Double-digit additions and removals for a change that added three lines.

steps.title: Highlight code that only moved
steps.why: `--color-moved` classifies each added line: genuinely new, or moved from elsewhere in the same diff. `--color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change` also forgives reindentation, which is what makes it work on real refactors.
steps.expect: The moved functions marked distinctly from the one genuinely new check.

steps.title: Choose a better algorithm
steps.why: `patience` and `histogram` produce diffs that align on distinctive lines rather than the shortest edit script. On reordered or heavily indented code they routinely turn a 60-line diff into a 6-line one.
commands: sh -c 'echo default:   $(git show HEAD~2 --numstat -- service.py | tail -1)'
sh -c 'echo patience:  $(git show HEAD~2 --patience --numstat -- service.py | tail -1)'
sh -c 'echo histogram: $(git show HEAD~2 --histogram --numstat -- service.py | tail -1)'
steps.expect: Different line counts for the same commit — same content, better alignment.

steps.title: Make the better algorithm your default
steps.why: `diff.algorithm histogram` applies it to every diff, log and show. There is no downside worth worrying about: it is marginally slower and consistently more readable.

verify.label: a more readable diff algorithm is the default

steps.title: Ignore whitespace-only churn
steps.why: The settings reformat changed alignment and nothing else. `-w` ignores whitespace entirely; `--ignore-blank-lines` handles the other common source of fake churn. Together they answer 'did anything actually change'.
steps.expect: Three changed lines normally, and completely empty output with -w — proof the commit was cosmetic. (Use `git diff` rather than `git show` for this test: show prints the commit header even when the diff is empty.)

verify.label: the reformat commit contains no real change
verify.hint: git diff -w between the two commits proves a diff is whitespace-only

steps.title: Show which function each hunk is in
steps.why: `--function-context` expands every hunk to the whole function containing it, so you review a change in its context rather than through a three-line window. Expensive to read, invaluable on unfamiliar code.

steps.title: Record the settings so the team benefits
steps.why: Algorithm and move detection are per-clone config, so put the lines in your contributing guide. A reviewer reading a moved-code diff without these flags will comment on things that did not change.

write.content:
# Contributing

Run these once per clone so refactor diffs are readable:

    git config diff.algorithm histogram
    git config diff.colorMoved zebra
    git config diff.colorMovedWS allow-indentation-change

When reviewing a reformat, check it with `git show -w` before commenting.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Document the diff settings reviewers should use"

verify.label: moved-code highlighting is on by default
the settings are documented for everyone else
a readable diff algorithm is configured
…and forgives reindentation, which is what makes it useful
you can prove the reformat commit changed nothing real
verify.hint: git diff -w between the commit and its parent

verify.label: the reviewer settings are written down

pitfalls: `--color-moved` only works with colour enabled. In a pipe or a script add `-c color.ui=always`, or you will see nothing and conclude it does not work.
`-w` hides genuine whitespace bugs — in Python, YAML or Makefiles indentation IS the code. Use it to answer a question, not as a default.
Changing `diff.algorithm` does not change any commit. Diffs are computed at read time, so this is purely a display setting.
Reordering functions and changing them in the same commit defeats every one of these flags. The real fix is to split the commit.
`--numstat` is the scriptable form; `--stat` is the human one and truncates long paths.
cheatsheet: distinguish moved code from new code
align on distinctive lines, not the shortest edit
is there any real change at all
